sources.entry: Sandstorm - Personal server for running self-hosted apps easily and securely. (Demo, Source Code) Apache-2.0 C++/Shell

summary.one_liner: Sandstorm is a self-hostable web productivity suite implemented as a security-hardened web app package manager for running your own server.
summary.what_it_does: Sandstorm lets you install web apps for tasks such as creating documents, spreadsheets, blogs, git repositories and task lists on a server you run yourself. The README describes it as a security-hardened web app package manager, comparing installing apps to installing them on a phone. It is open source and is said to run on any x86-64 Linux system. The README points to external documentation for installation, usage, how it works and security practices, and for packaging apps through a developer hub. The README itself contains only overview text and links, with no detailed setup steps.
use_cases: run personal web server for documents and spreadsheets
host a blog or git repository privately
install web apps on a home server
package own web apps for Sandstorm
how_to_run: See installation instructions in the Sandstorm documentation
notable: Acts as a security-hardened web app package manager for self-hosted apps
Installs apps for documents, spreadsheets, blogs, git repos and task lists
Developer hub for packaging your own apps
Demo available to try before installing
caveats: Runs only on x86-64 Linux according to the README
Installation details are in external documentation rather than the README
keywords: run apps on my own server
install apps like on a phone
